translation_notes: Mechanical draft wrote `g += g{ {URIRef(base + "thing")} {URIRef(base + "ns#comment")} "anything" }` (the known add_isolated draft bias): rewritten as `@graph g` + `+{ }`, the construction the stratum targets.

The bare `<http://example.org/other>` / `<http://example.org/ns#Thing>` terms in the yielded tuples were already correct in the draft (IRI island used directly as a Python value, outside any g{ }/+{ } block) and are kept as-is.

The graph `g` built inside get_bind_tests is local to the generator and never returned or assigned at module level, so the driver cannot rely on run_pair's built-in entry=/calls= comparison (it would compare the yielded `check` NESTED FUNCTION objects with ==, which are never equal across two module executions -- a false FAIL unrelated to the translation). driver.py instead reaches the graph via `check.__closure__` (co_freevars == ('g',)) and compares it by isomorphism -- the true add_isolated oracle here.

The nested check() function's own `g.query("..." % expr)` (categories.sparql=1) was left as plain rdflib: `expr` there is spliced in as raw SPARQL clause TEXT (e.g. 'bind("thing" as ?name)'), not a term, and `s{ }` only interpolates `{expr}` in term position (never string pasting, per INSTRUCTIONS.md SS2). This region's `strata` is add_isolated only -- the tirage did not tag it sparql_literal/sparql_interpolated -- so this untouched call is scaffolding around the region under test, not a missed credit.
